A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KEDAS, despite v2's new title and substantial shift toward CRAFT. Both complete 14-page documents, including Appendices A–G, have readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original editing experiments across four datasets, three backbones and three settings, plus ablations, efficiency measurements and general-task evaluations.

after.justification: v2 reports original CRAFT exposure measurements, editing comparisons and ablations in Tables 2, 5 and 6, alongside retained traditional-benchmark results.

M1.justification: KEDAS changes from selecting one filtered edit to jointly prompting with up to three edits (v1 Equations 14–15; v2 Equations 13–14). CRAFT also introduces alias augmentation and paired-edit alignment/filter training constructions. Paraphrased and reversed augmentation remains for traditional benchmarks in Appendix G. These substantially adapt the retained LoRA and adaptive-routing framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds CRAFT-Statistics and CRAFT-Finance, covering Chinese numerical knowledge, paired-edit calculations, aliases, temporal locality and C3-based general locality. MQuAKE and EvoWiki enter the exposure analysis. The four traditional editing datasets remain in Appendix G, but CommonsenseQA, MNLI, MMLU and SST evaluations disappear.

E2.justification: The evaluated suite drops MEND, SERAC, RECIPE and AlphaEdit. LoRA and ROME, evaluated only under single editing in v1, enter v2's sequential CRAFT comparison alongside IKE, EREN, WISE and LTE. The comparator membership in the retained Llama-3.1 traditional-benchmark comparison is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 restricts editing evaluation to Llama-3.1 and sequential editing. CRAFT introduces 500 test instances per subset and five separate metrics; KEDAS uses eight retrieval candidates and three adopted edits, versus four candidates and one adopted edit in v1. Appendix G also changes the stated legacy alignment-data source from reused LTE data to dataset-specific construction; the identical reported scores do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds the five-model benchmark-exposure analysis and replaces the earlier component ablations with CRAFT ablations, omitting the no-alignment condition. v1's comparative cost analysis, general-capability retention tests, DEA transfer to LTE, output case study, LTE shot-count comparison and unsuccessful triplet-augmentation analysis are absent.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly states that every method is run once. v2 retains the deterministic-generation and disabled-sampling statements but omits the run count. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds CRAFT exposure, editing and ablation results. For example, Table 5 reports composite portability of 81.20 and 55.95 for KEDAS, versus 68.58 and 50.21 for LTE on Statistics and Finance. These are new-setting results. All 75 values in v2 Table 9 match v1 Table 4's Llama-3.1 block, while numerous other backbone, setting and diagnostic results disappear.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the formal paired-edit requirement for composite portability and revises the selected-edit definition from a single argmax to a top-k set. v1's explicit filter-loss equations 16–20 are omitted in favor of a training-data construction. Neither version contains theorems, proofs or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion shift from a broadly validated KEDAS method to CRAFT as a central contribution, emphasizing updateability, low exposure and composite editing. v1's headline claims about winning 35 of 36 configurations, transferable augmentation and comparative efficiency are replaced by claims about CRAFT's challenges and KEDAS's performance on it.

C2.justification: v2 interprets low exposure as supporting benchmark fairness and attributes weaker Finance temporal locality to possible filter generalization failures. Limitations now emphasize Chinese/domain coverage, two-hop reasoning, annual financial updates and one editing backbone. v1's one-hop restriction and augmentation-provider dependence disappear, as do interpretations supported by its efficiency, general-task and transfer analyses.

D1.justification: v2 supplies CRAFT collection sources and APIs, update instructions, a revised code/data location, alignment/filter training recipes and Chinese augmentation prompts. Earlier filter-sample counts and detailed baseline checkpoint/compatibility information disappear. The Llama-3.1 LoRA hyperparameters remain identical, while the reported training and editing times now describe CRAFT.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark positioning around MQuAKE, WikiBigEdit, EvoWiki, Sanitation and HalluEditBench, contrasting CRAFT's updateability and reasoning coverage with prior datasets. v1's separate language-model alignment review, including PPO, DPO and GRPO, is removed. This substantially changes the research context beyond citation or bibliography formatting.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list and conclusion are extensively rewritten around CRAFT. A dedicated dataset section precedes the retained method, sections become numbered, limitations and ethics receive separate sections, and the appendices are reorganized around CRAFT construction and examples instead of the earlier diagnostic suite.

P2.justification: New benchmark-comparison, exposure, dataset-statistics and CRAFT-result tables replace much of the earlier experimental presentation. The retained Llama-3.1 results move into a compact appendix table. Figure 1 is revised for aliases and multiple adopted edits, and the appendix prompt figures are substantially replaced and reduced.

improvement.justification: CRAFT and joint multi-edit inference add useful domain and compositional evidence, addressing v1's single-edit portability restriction. However, v2 removes validation across multiple backbones and settings, controlled efficiency comparisons, general-task retention tests and transfer analyses. Its new exposure-rate claims also lack a specified scoring procedure. These substantial gains and losses leave the net direction of overall paper quality unclear.
